**Iceland signs up to TIPS, extending euro instant payments infrastructure beyond the eurozone**

*The ECB and Iceland's central bank have agreed to connect the Icelandic króna to TIPS from 2028, making Iceland the latest non-euro country to join Europe's instant settlement infrastructure.*

The agreement, announced on June 24, will allow payments in Icelandic króna to settle instantly in central bank money through the Eurosystem's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement system. Iceland joins Denmark and Sweden, which connected to TIPS as part of the ECB's cross-currency instant payments initiative launched earlier this month.

The move reflects the ECB's strategy of positioning TIPS as a pan-European settlement layer that extends well beyond the euro area. For Iceland, it brings domestic instant payments onto shared infrastructure rather than building in isolation. The 2028 go-live date suggests a substantial technical integration ahead, but the political commitment is now formal.

The broader pattern is clear: TIPS is becoming the default instant settlement backbone for European currencies, euro or otherwise. Each new entrant strengthens the network effects that make it harder for alternative approaches to compete.

*Sources: [Iceland joins TIPS for instant payments](https://www.ecb.europa.eu//press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260624_1~ce8e85127f.en.html) — European Central Bank | [Iceland to join Target Instant Payment Settlement System](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47983/iceland-to-join-target-instant-payment-settlement-system) — Finextra*

**FCA chief signals open banking collaboration and AI as priorities in regulatory rethink**

*The FCA has set out its thinking on how regulation must adapt to AI, with specific implications for open banking, open finance and competition policy.*

In a speech published on June 24, the FCA addressed how artificial intelligence is reshaping the case for regulatory intervention. The regulator explicitly referenced open banking, noting that it has "considered the case for beneficial collaboration under competition law, so commercial Variable Recurring Payments can get off the ground." That framing — treating VRP adoption as a problem partly of coordination, not just competition — marks a notable shift in tone.

The speech also positioned open finance as an area where the FCA sees a facilitation role for itself, suggesting the regulator views data-sharing frameworks as requiring active stewardship rather than purely market-led development. This aligns with the FCA's earlier open finance roadmap but adds specificity around AI's intersection with those frameworks.

For firms building on open banking rails or preparing for open finance requirements, the speech signals that the FCA is willing to flex competition norms where it sees coordination failures holding back adoption. That has practical consequences for how industry bodies and scheme operators structure VRP rollouts.

*Sources: [Rethinking regulation for the age of AI](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/speeches/rethinking-regulation-age-ai) — FCA*

**Worldpay outage disrupts UK card payments during World Cup match**

*Worldpay suffered a service outage on the evening of June 24, leaving some UK merchants unable to process card payments during the England v Ghana World Cup game.*

The outage hit pubs and retailers during a peak spending window, with reports of failed card transactions across multiple locations. Worldpay, owned by Global Payments following its 2025 acquisition from GTCR, is one of the UK's largest payment processors and handles a significant share of in-store card volume.

High-profile outages during major events expose the concentration risk inherent in payment processing. The UK's reliance on a small number of acquirers and processors means that a single point of failure can have outsized effects on commerce. The incident will likely feed into ongoing industry discussions about resilience standards and the case for diversifying payment acceptance methods, including account-to-account alternatives that bypass card processing infrastructure entirely.

*Sources: [Worldpay suffers outage during England vs Ghana World Cup game](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47988/worldpay-suffers-outage-during-england-vs-ghana-world-cup-game) — Finextra*

**PayPoint completes AperiData acquisition to build open banking into credit data**

*PayPoint has completed its acquisition of AperiData, a UK credit reference agency with an open banking platform, following a previous strategic investment.*

The deal gives PayPoint direct ownership of a real-time credit data capability built on open banking rails. AperiData's platform allows lenders and other organisations to access bank transaction data for affordability assessments and creditworthiness checks, combining traditional credit reference agency functions with open banking data ingestion.

The acquisition sits within a broader consolidation pattern in the UK open banking data market. As open banking matures from payment initiation into data-driven decisioning, firms that can combine regulated credit data with real-time bank account information hold an increasingly valuable position. PayPoint's move reflects the commercial logic of vertically integrating these capabilities rather than relying on third-party open banking providers.

*Sources: [PayPoint completes AperiData acquisition to strengthen Open Banking capabilities](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/paypoint-completes-aperidata-acquisition-to-strengthen-open-banking-capabilities/) — Open Banking Expo | [PayPoint acquires Aperidata](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47980/paypoint-acquires-aperidata) — Finextra*

**Mastercard and PrivatBank complete Ukraine's first AI agent payment**

*Mastercard's Agent Pay product has been used to execute Ukraine's first payment initiated by an AI agent, extending the technology's deployment into a new European market.*

The transaction, completed in partnership with PrivatBank, Ukraine's largest retail bank, used Mastercard's Agent Pay framework to allow an AI agent to initiate and complete a payment autonomously. The announcement follows Mastercard's earlier agentic payment demonstration with ING and Worldline in early June, and Visa's parallel partnership with OpenAI.

Agentic payments are moving rapidly from concept to live deployment. The pace of market-by-market rollouts suggests the card networks view AI-initiated transactions as a near-term product category rather than a long-horizon experiment. The choice of Ukraine, a market with high digital payment adoption driven partly by the conflict, underscores how agentic commerce is being tested across diverse conditions rather than confined to Western European pilot markets.

*Sources: [Mastercard and PrivatBank complete Ukraine's first payment executed by an AI agent](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110244/mastercard-and-privatbank-complete-ukraines-first-payment-executed-by-an-ai-agent) — Finextra*
